title: From Hormuz to data centers: How Iran’s threats are raising stakes of renewed war
gist: Iranian officials say another war would carry prohibitive costs: Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei threatens a broader target list including Gulf energy infrastructure and AI facilities, as Tehran tries to turn vulnerability into deterrent leverage.

insights.claim: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned that Iran has a broader target list for another round of fighting, potentially including Gulf energy infrastructure and artificial intelligence facilities.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Gulf data centers and energy assets are explicitly in Iranian threat rhetoric, relevant to AI-infrastructure siting and energy risk premia.

insights.claim: Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf is highlighting the economic and military costs Washington would bear if war resumes.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Deterrence messaging aimed at US domestic cost sensitivity.

insights.claim: Tehran is trying to turn its vulnerability to renewed attack into leverage, but it must convince adversaries that escalation is prohibitively expensive without provoking the confrontation it says it is preparing for.
insights.speaker: A correspondent in Tehran
insights.so_what: Rhetorical escalation raises tail risk of miscalculation; watch for threat-to-action transitions.
